Karthik / Neha — forwarding Crestwell's redlines. Key ask: carve out personal injury and property damage from our liability cap. Procurement is pushing because they have on-site gear and contractor work.

My read: personal injury carve-outs are unusual for pure SaaS but this customer has an on-site element. I don't want to accept an uncapped carve-out. Proposed approach:

- Limit the carve-out to (i) bodily injury and (ii) direct physical damage to the customer's tangible property caused by Redwood personnel while performing on-site services;
- Apply a sub-cap (e.g., $1,000,000) for that carve-out (separate from the general cap);
- Require Crestwell to accept that consequential damages stay excluded;
- Certificate of insurance (general liability, tech E&O where applicable) and proof of worker's comp for onsite staff before the first deployment.

Can you draft suggested redline language or flag legal risk if we should say no? Also loop in pricing if we need to increase the standard cap for this account.

Thanks — Laura

Laura / Neha — quick legal take.

Summary:
- We should avoid an unlimited carve-out. For SaaS-only customers we typically refuse personal injury/property carve-outs; with on-site work we can accept a narrow, controlled exception tied to Redwood's negligence while performing on-site services.
- Recommended language (high level): carve-out applies only to "bodily injury and direct physical damage to tangible property" where the injury/damage is caused by Redwood (or its agents) during the provision of on-site installation or hardware maintenance. Exclude claims that are consequential or economic loss.
- Cap: a sub-limit (I suggest $1m–$2m depending on exposure). Practically, $1,000,000 is reasonable and aligns with our commercial insurance. If Crestwell insists on a higher sub-cap, ask Pricing for gross margin impact and consider a one-time fee or higher MRR.
- Insurance: require Crestwell to receive a certificate of insurance naming Redwood as an additional insured for on-site work (general liability) and confirm worker's comp for onsite personnel. If the work is performed by a partner/vendor, require evidence of vendor insurance.
- Indemnity: avoid creating broad third-party bodily injury indemnities. If Crestwell insists, limit to Redwood's negligence and exclude punitive damages.

Proposed redline snippet to include in Order Form / Exhibit A: 
"Notwithstanding the foregoing limitation of liability, claims for bodily injury or direct physical damage to tangible property caused by Redwood personnel while performing on-site services shall not be subject to the general liability cap but shall be subject to a sub-limit of $1,000,000 per incident and in the aggregate. This exception shall not apply to consequential, special, or economic losses. Customer shall provide proof of insurance and name Redwood as an additional insured for on-site services prior to commencement."

I'll paste a cleaned-up version for Laura to send to Crestwell. Also flag: if Crestwell's contract requires site-specific indemnities or unlimited remedies, escalate.

—Karthik

Sofia — thanks for sending the redlines. We're happy to move forward but we need to narrow the carve-out and put objective limits in place so both sides are protected. Please see the summary below and the attached redlined Order Form (highlighted changes).

What Redwood can accept:
- A limited carve-out for (i) bodily injury and (ii) direct physical damage to tangible property that is caused by Redwood personnel while performing on-site services under the Order Form.
- That carve-out will be subject to a sub-limit of $1,000,000 per incident and in the aggregate.
- Consequential, incidental, special, and economic losses remain excluded per the MSA.
- Crestwell must provide a certificate of insurance (general liability and worker's comp) naming Redwood as an additional insured for on-site activities before any on-site work commences. If third-party contractors perform the work, Crestwell must produce vendor insurance evidence.

If Crestwell wants a higher sub-cap, let me know and we can route to Pricing for a commercial exception. Otherwise, if you accept the language above we can finalize and sign.

Attached: Crestwell_Order_Form_v3_redlines.pdf (our redline), Exhibit-A-liability-comp.xlsx (cap comparison)
